title: Clock skew in SAML assertions causing session reconciliation permission flaps
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported intermittent 'permission denied' errors followed by transient over-permissioned access windows after SSO/SAML reauthentication. Root cause appears to be clock-skew handling between Identity Providers (IdPs) and our SSO assertion TTL reconciliation logic, which can cause stale role assertions to be treated as both expired and then re-applied in a way that bypasses audit metadata updates. Impact: users experience denial of critical admin actions for 10-30s, then in some cases find elevated permissions persisted without proper audit entries. Repro: 1) Configure IdP with non-zero clock skew (AWS/Okta tests used 45s offset). 2) Login to Redwood Console, trigger SAML SSO refresh token path. 3) Rapidly perform role-change activity (invite, role-edit) while session reconciliation is happening. 4) Observe: one request receives 403; subsequent requests within ~20s return 200 for admin-only endpoints. Also note missing or partial audit log entries (missing correlation_id and original_assertion timestamp). Hypothesis: our session reconciliation logic uses an 'assertion_valid_at' timestamp that is normalized incorrectly when IdP timestamp + skew lands < now by a small margin. The code path tries to refresh roles but merges claims without invalidating cached RBAC bindings atomically, and audit logging is emitted only on successful reconciliation, not on cache invalidation. Fix approach: 1) Treat incoming SAML assertion timestamps with explicit clock-skew tolerance window (configurable, default 120s) but ensure deterministically ordered reconciliation steps: validate assertion -> compute delta -> perform atomic binding update with optimistic locking -> emit audit entries for both invalidation and new bindings. 2) Add a reconciliation fence in session manager to prevent parallel reconcile flows for same session id. 3) Add test harness that simulates IdP clock skew and concurrent role operations. 4) Emit an explicit audit record when an assertion is rejected due to TTL/clock-skew and include original_assertion_ts, received_ts, and applied_skew_tolerance. Acceptance criteria: - Repro steps above fail to produce permission flaps in CI harness and in canary customer environment. - Audit logs consistently contain both invalidation and new binding records with correlation_id. - No user-visible 403->200 flips observed in canary for 48 hours. - Add telemetry: count of reconciliation races and count of assertions rejected for TTL/clock reasons, surfaced in Console. Rollback plan: revert reconciliation fence and binding update atomically if downstream errors; temporarily increase skew tolerance to reduce customer impact while patch is staged. Security review required: yes. Release target: runtime-1.20. Additional notes: this touches RBAC binding cache, session manager, and audit pipeline (kafka topic audit-events). Coordinate with infra to ensure audit pipeline retention for debug window during rollout.
comments: 2025-08-12 Sofia Martinez: Created ticket after Customer A escalation and initial triage. Captured live logs and partial audit events showing missing correlation_id.
2025-08-13 Liam O'Connor: Reproduced locally using Okta test account with 45s clock offset. Confirmed 403->200 flip and audit gap. Started sketching fix for reconciliation fence.
2025-08-15 Engineering sync: Agreed on optimism locking + fence. PM requested telemetry counters and Console dashboard row for reconciliation incidents.
2025-08-18 PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8124 - initial atomic binding update + fence implementation. CI included new SAML clock-skew harness.

2025-08-20 Review note from Security (Aisha Patel): Must include explicit audit entry for rejected assertions and mark security_review_required true. Also asked for threat model note about persistent overgrant if audit pipeline falls behind.

2025-08-22 QA: Canary deployed to customer B (non-prod) for 24h. No flaps observed; audit entries present. Observed a spike in 'reconciliation_race' telemetry; investigating edge where parallel refresh and role mutation collide.
2025-08-24 Release prep: Added config flag SAML_CLOCK_SKEW_TOLERANCE default 120. Ops to enable additional logging for 72h post-release.
